newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Avesta Sheffield says one-off costs last quarter.
newsitem.headline: Avesta Sheffield says one-off costs last quarter.

text.p: Swedish-British steel group Avesta Sheffield said on Thursday that it had significant one-off costs in the last quarter of its 1996/1997 financial year.

"For the financial year's last quarter pre-tax profit amounted to 12 million crowns after significant one-off costs," the company said in a statement, adding that the costs, partly related to restructuring, amounted to 150 million crowns.
For the full financial year the group swung to a pre-tax loss of 124 million crowns from a pre-tax profit of 3.60 billion crowns.

"The fall in profit between 1995/1996 and 1996/1997 is due primarily to the negative market conditions -- falls in sales prices for nearly all products, exchange rate changes and price changes in inventory," it said.
"It was also affected by excess costs of commissioning new plants and substantial one off items."
Foreign exchange fluctuations hurt the full year result by 300 million crowns, the company's financial officer David Gabriel told a telephone conference.
The result was lower than expected with analysts in a Reuter poll targeting a pre-tax profit of 16 million crowns.

The report pushed Avesta Sheffield's share somewhat lower on the Stockholm Stock Exchange, down 0.5 crown at 84.5 at 1510 GMT. Earlier, before the figures were released, the share was changing hands at 85.5 crowns.
When looking ahead, Avesta Sheffield saw risks for a buildup of inventories.
"Demand and order intake for most products are currently at a high level, with an accompanying risk of an inventory build-up," the company said.
"Avesta Sheffield is confident that there will be strong market growth for 1997/1998 as a whole but maintains a cautious position on the sustainability of the current pace of growth."
Prices increases have been obtained for June deliveries, but the fact that major producers in the U.S. have abandoned proposed price rises in May does not bode well for maintaining them, it said.
"Part of the benefit from price rises will be offset by the effects of the stronger pound and dollar," the company said.
During the first quarter order intake was strong and prices rose, it said.
Full-year sales dropped 21 percent to 17.2 billion crowns from the previous financial year and the company proposed a one crown dividend.
In the fifteen month period 1995/96, the dividend amounted to three crowns.
